subject: AuroraRetail SLO & scaling: hosted vs. dedicated decision recap
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@auroraretail.com>, ops@auroraretail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AuroraRetail SLO & scaling: hosted vs. dedicated decision recap

Hi Lina / Aurora ops team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and what we recommend as next steps so everyone has the same view.

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Primary workload: search + personalization during checkout (single-token + short-context generation)
- Sustained baseline: ~30 qps (search + personalization combined)
- Promotion peaks: up to ~200 qps for short bursts (3-10 min) during flash sales
- Latency target: P95 <= 150ms end-to-end for the search call (including network)
- Data posture: no on-prem requirement for initial pilot; PCI-scope concerns for payment tokens later in flow

What this means for deployment mode:
- Hosted API: fast to start, no infra commitment. Works fine for baseline and moderate peaks if you rely on burst capacity, but you may see variability in P95 during large, simultaneous bursts. Good for quick pilot and early validation.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools give predictable P95 and capacity headroom to absorb 200 qps peaks without needing routing fallbacks. Recommended for production if you need strict latency SLOs and throughput guarantees.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): only necessary if you need control for PCI or strict data residency — not required for the pilot.

Recommended next steps:
1) Start a 2-week proof-of-concept on Hosted with an agreed load script (we'll replay a 10x scaled promotion profile) so we can measure observed P95 and tail behavior.
2) Parallel sizing assessment for a Dedicated configuration that would meet 150ms P95 during 200 qps peaks — we'll provide a cost delta and concrete sizing options (1x, 2x redundancy).
3) If SLOs are met on Hosted during pilot, evaluate a short-term Dedicated reservation for production cutover (we can do a canary roll).

Attachments I’m sharing: aurora_slo_matrix.xlsx (matrix of measured vs. target latency by qps), pilot_cost_estimate.pdf (prelim cost ranges).

Can you confirm the peak profile (200 qps is aggregate across all regions?) and whether there are any additional endpoints that need sub-150ms SLOs? Once you confirm, we’ll schedule the pilot start and lock in the load script.

Thanks —
Michael

From: Lina Park <lina.park@auroraretail.com>

Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AuroraRetail SLO & scaling: hosted vs. dedicated decision recap

On Tue, Dec 8, 2026 at 09:12 AM Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call this morning...

Thanks, Michael — this summary is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- The 200 qps peak is aggregate for our North America checkout cluster (single region). We have a second region with much lower volume (~10 qps) that we can treat separately.
- The 30 qps baseline is correct for daytime traffic; overnight is closer to 3-5 qps.
- The sub-150ms SLO applies only to the search recommendation endpoint used in-cart. Other personalization endpoints can tolerate up to 300ms P95.

Procurement note: we are evaluating two options — a short pilot without any long-term financial commitment, and a production plan with a 12-month reserved capacity commitment (if Dedicated pricing looks reasonable). They asked whether Redwood can provide a preliminary annual TCO estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted (with committed burst credits).

I attached our internal SLO doc (Aurora-SLO-reqs.pdf) — happy to add any additional detail you need. Let us know the earliest you can start the pilot window; we prefer the week of Dec 14 if possible.

Cheers,
Lina Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora Retail
lina.park@auroraretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AuroraRetail SLO & scaling: hosted vs. dedicated decision recap

Michael — copying Ben to pull pricing and sizing. Quick internal note and proposed send to Aurora: 

Option A — Hosted pilot (recommended start):
- 2-week load test using Hosted with an imposed promotion profile (we can replay logs at 10x scale for headroom testing).
- Pros: fastest to start, no infra commit, Redwood handles autoscaling.
- Cons: potential P95 variance during simultaneous global bursts; we’ll measure tail.
- Estimated pilot cost (2 weeks, test load as described): see pilot_cost_estimate.pdf (approx $3.5k–$6k depending on replay intensity).

Option B — Dedicated for production (recommended if Aurora requires firm P95 for 200 qps):
- Suggested baseline config: 2 dedicated worker pools (N+1) sized to sustain 200 qps at target latencies with room for KV cache warmups.
- Pros: predictable latency/SLOs, isolation, easier root-cause for tail events.
- Cons: higher monthly commitment.
- Preliminary annual TCO (ballpark): will share brackets — low/mid/high based on model family and quantization. Ben, can you prepare the 12-month TCO ranges + uplift for redundancy?

Option C — Private/VPC: only if PCI scoping requires it; we’ll treat as a separate track and need security checklist.

Action items I will send to Aurora in the reply: confirm pilot start week (Dec 14), ask for sample logs (for replay), and provide conservative Dedicated sizing options plus an initial TCO bracket.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Lead, Sales
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AuroraRetail SLO & scaling: hosted vs. dedicated decision recap

Lina —

Thanks for the confirmation and for sending Aurora-SLO-reqs.pdf. We can start the Hosted pilot the week of Dec 14; proposed timeline below.

Proposed schedule:
- Dec 14: kickoff + instrumentation checklist (we’ll provide a short SDK snippet for latency tagging).
- Dec 15–17: sample-data replay and sanity tests at 1x–5x.
- Dec 18–21: full promotion-profile replay window (includes 10x spike test).
- Dec 22: results review and recommendation (Hosted viability vs Dedicated sizing).

Deliverables we’ll provide:
- Measured P95/P99 latency matrix by endpoint (attached: aurora_slo_matrix.xlsx).
- Pilot cost summary (pilot_cost_estimate.pdf).
- Dedicated sizing options and 12-month TCO brackets (Ben will follow up).

If that timeline works, please confirm and share a small sample of production logs (anonymized) and a preferred DocuSign contact for the pilot MSA. I’ll send a compact MSA for the pilot (no long-term commit) and a DocuSign link once you confirm.

DocuSign preview: https://app.redwood.com/pilot/msas/aurora/2026

Best,
Michael Grant | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
